newsitem.title: UK: Right diet can cut jail violence - expert.
newsitem.headline: Right diet can cut jail violence - expert.

text.p: Violence in prisons can be cut by half if inmates are given a balanced diet, a leading expert said on Tuesday after studying convicts in the United States.
Professor Stephen Schoenthaler from California State University's Department of Sociology and Criminal Justice researched the effect of diet in more than 100 jails.

"We have been able to cut institutional violence just about in half by making sure that prisoners, inmates, delinquents have a diet that is consistent with the recommendations of the World Health Organisation, the British health authorities and the National Academy of Science in the U.S.," Schoenthaler told a conference on nutrition.
He said inmates in the studies had shortages of 14 or 15 nutrients, including many vitamins and some minerals.

"We can lower aggression either by giving them a proper balanced diet and we can also do it by leaving the diet alone and just by giving them a low dose of a very good multiple mineral supplement," said Schoenthaler.
He said the trend towards juvenile delinquency could be reversed in eight to 10 year olds if more attention was paid to their diets.
